title: Normality ascends along flat maps of Noetherian rings with normal fibres
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that (1) $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], (2) $S$ is Noetherian, (3) $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], (4) for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and (5) $R$ is a normal ring. Then $S$ is a normal ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541) and its proof: Serre's criterion, Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal: a Noetherian ring is normal iff it has (R_1) and (S_2)), with Lemma Tag 0339 (lemma-Sk-goes-up) and Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up)

proof.text: *The fibre rings are Noetherian.* Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal. Since $S$ is Noetherian (hypothesis (2)), the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. So every fibre ring is a Noetherian ring which is normal by hypothesis (4), and the conditions $(R_k)$, $(S_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], defined for Noetherian rings, make sense for it.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541), proof ('Thus we know $R$ and the fibre rings have these properties'; Stacks leaves implicit that the fibre rings are Noetherian, which Serre's criterion requires)

proof.text: *$R$ and the fibre rings have $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$.* By Serre's criterion [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal], direction normal $\Rightarrow$ $(R_1)+(S_2)$, applied to the Noetherian normal ring $R$ (hypotheses (1) and (5)) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $R$ has properties $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]. Applied to each fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, which is Noetherian (step 1) and normal (hypothesis (4)), it shows that every fibre ring has $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541), proof, first two sentences, with Lemma Tag 031S (lemma-criterion-normal)

proof.text: *$S$ has $(S_2)$.* The ring map $\varphi:R\to S$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], the fibre rings have $(S_2)$ and $R$ has $(S_2)$ (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-serre-sk-goes-up] with $k=2$, $S$ has property $(S_2)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541), proof, third sentence, with Lemma Tag 0339 (lemma-Sk-goes-up)

proof.text: *$S$ has $(R_1)$.* Under the same hypotheses, the fibre rings have $(R_1)$ and $R$ has $(R_1)$ (step 2); here $(R_1)$ of [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] is the property stated in [lem-weil-pbc-regularity-rk-goes-up] (every localization at a prime of height $\le1$ is a regular local ring). By [lem-weil-pbc-regularity-rk-goes-up] with $k=1$, $S$ has property $(R_1)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian, line 46541), proof, third sentence, with Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $S$ is a Noetherian ring (hypothesis (2)) with properties $(R_1)$ (step 4) and $(S_2)$ (step 3). By Serre's criterion [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal], direction $(R_1)+(S_2)\Rightarrow$ normal, $S$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].
